studies.title: Phase II trial of thymosin fraction 5 and thymosin alpha 1.
studies.abstract: Previous Phase I trials have established the safety of administering thymosin fraction 5 and thymosin alpha 1 to patients with advanced cancer. These same trials also suggested potential immune-enhancing doses of these agents. In this study, 12 patients with colon cancer were treated with thrice weekly thymosin fraction 5 at a dose of 120 mg/m2, and 10 patients with non-small-cell lung cancer received thymosin alpha 1 at 1.2 mg/m2 thrice weekly. Five patients with hypernephroma also received one or both agents by a thrice weekly schedule. There were no tumor responses observed in any of these patients, and immune enhancement was neither obtained nor sustained. We conclude that at these doses and schedules, these hormones have very limited, if any, antitumor properties and that they are incapable of producing immune augmentation as defined by the assays used in this study.

studies.title: The Immunomodulatory Activity of Thymosin Alpha 1 on Tumor Cell Lines and Distinct Immune Cell Subsets.
studies.abstract:
Background

The immune-balancing role of thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1) is well-recognized in contexts of immune dysregulation. Within the anti-tumor context, Tα1 demonstrated to act as an immune-enhancer, with potential roles in immunotherapy-based treatments. However, Tα1 immunomodulatory potential on tumor cells is poorly understood. Additionally, Tα1 pleiotropic effects on immune cells require in-depth investigations to unravel its specific impact on different immune cell populations. Thus, we first aimed to investigate whether Tα1 treatments influenced the transcriptional immune profile of various cancer cell lines. Alongside, CD4+ T, CD8+ T, B, and natural killer cells from healthy donors (HDs) were treated individually with Tα1, to assess its direct effects on each immune cell population.

Methods

Cutaneous melanoma, glioblastoma, and pleural mesothelioma cell lines and HD immune cell subsets were treated with Tα1 for 48 hours. Total RNA was subsequently isolated, and gene expression profiles were analyzed by the nCounter® SPRINT Profiler. Genes with a log2ratio ≥0.58 and ≤-0.58 in Tα1-treated vs untreated cells were defined as differentially expressed (DEGs) and subsequently evaluated for the enrichment of Gene Ontology terms to identify biological processes potentially affected by Tα1 in tumor and immune cells.

Results

Tα1 minimally changed cancer cell DEGs and immune-related biological processes, suggesting a comprehensive lack of transcriptional immunomodulatory potential on the tumor counterpart. Conversely, Tα1 exhibited to directly affect the proliferation and/or transcription processes of each studied immune cell subset, with the greatest transcriptional impact observed for activated CD8+ T cells, crucial players in anti-tumor immunity.

Conclusion

Our findings question the tumor immunomodulatory properties of Tα1, simultaneously underscoring the importance of further investigating Tα1 influence on specific immune cell subsets in the periphery or within the tumor microenvironment of cancer patients. This would contribute to understand Tα1 potential in immunotherapy-based combination strategies, within the anti-tumor setting.

studies.title: Immunological effects of heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy can be augmented by thymosin α1.
studies.abstract: Peritoneal metastases of colorectal carcinoma origin (PM-CRC) are treated by cytoreductive surgery and heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). However, the majority of patients recur, calling for novel treatments. We explored the immunogenic changes induced by HIPEC and the possibility to use thymosin α1 (Tα1) as an immune-stimulatory agent. We used an experimental murine model of PM-CRC combined with mitomycin (MMC)-based HIPEC. We determined immune cell infiltration into tumor metastases after HIPEC administration by means of immunohistochemistry, and determined immunogenic cell death signals in tumor cells by real-time polymerase chain reaction. Mice with PM-CRC treated by HIPEC had increased overall survival (OS) compared to sham-treated mice (median OS 22.8 vs 18.9 days, respectively; P < 0.001). HIPEC induced increased infiltration of CD4+, CD8+, CD68 + and CD20 + cells into omental and visceral metastases at a magnitude of 40-100 %. We searched for potential immune signals induced by HIPEC by determining its effects on known immunogenic cell death proteins (heat-shock protein [HSP]-70, HSP-90 and calreticulin). HIPEC significantly increased HSP-90 mRNA expression (2.37 ± 1.5 vs 1-fold change, P < 0.05). The OS of Tα1 treated mice significantly improved compared to HIPEC-treated mice (16.3 ± 0.8 vs 14.1 ± 0.6 days, respectively, P = 0.02) and vs sham (11.8 ± 0.8 days, P = 0.007). HIPEC induced immunogenic changes that led to increased immune cell infiltration. These changes were further augmented by Tα1 treatment. Future studies aimed at optimizing Tα1 treatment should focus upon the immune response it evokes.

studies.title: Thymosin alpha 1 as an adjuvant to hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in an experimental model of peritoneal metastases from colonic carcinoma.
studies.abstract: Heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) is currently implemented in the treatment of peritoneal metastases from colorectal carcinoma (PM-CRC) origin. However, recurrence is common and the effectiveness of HIPEC has been questioned. The aim of this study was to evaluate the use of thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1), an immunomodulatory molecule, as an adjuvant to HIPEC treatment. We developed an experimental model of HIPEC by the induction of PM-CRC in C57BL mice and intra-abdominal perfusion of mitomycin C (MMC). Mice were treated with Tα1 at 0.6 mg/kg for 5 days after HIPEC. Clinical and immunological parameters were compared between HIPEC and HIPEC + Tα1 groups. Treatment with Tα1 increased overall survival of mice compared to HIPEC treatment alone and sham-treated animals (16.1 ± 0.8 vs. 14.1 ± 0.6 and 11.8 ± 0.8, respectively, p = 0.02). Tα1 had no direct anti-tumor effect, as seen by lack of inhibition of tumor cell proliferation. Tα1 treatment induced a T helper (Th) 1 immune response in tumor metastases as evidenced by a significant increase of the Th1-specific markers IFN-γ and T-bet (1.21 ± 0.3 vs. 0.52 ± 0.08, p < 0.05; 0.88 ± 0.04 vs. 0.64 ± 0.14, p < 0.05, respectively). This Th1 skew was accompanied by increased CD8 Tα1 augments the effect of HIPEC by the induction of a Th1 anti-tumor immune response. Further experiments should evaluate Tα1 and other novel immunomodulators in order to exploit the immunological opportunities created by HIPEC.

studies.title: Combination of Gemcitabine and Thymosin alpha 1 exhibit a better anti-tumor effect on nasal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma.
studies.abstract: Nasal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NNKTL) is an aggressive and poor prognostic malignant tumor along with high-level infection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Gemcitabine (Gem) and Thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1) exert an anti-tumor effect in various cancers. However, the effect of the combination of Gem and Tα1 in NNKTL remains unknown. SNK6 cells were treated with Gem, Tα1 and Gem plus Tα1 for 48 h. The expression levels of EBV and inflammatory factors were measured by qRT-PCR assay. The effect of Gem and Tα1 on cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, autophagy was detected by CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, autophagic flux measurement, respectively. Western blot was used to evaluate the expression of proteins related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), apoptosis and autophagy. In vivo xenograft models were used to further verify the roles of Gem and Tα1. Tumors were removed for weight measurement, H&E and IHC staining. We identified that the half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of Gem and Tα1 was 116.5 μmol/ml and 1.334 μmol/ml. Alone or combined administration of Gem and Tα1 dramatically attenuated the EBV viral load and promoted inflammatory factors expression in SNK6 cells, among which the combination of Gem and Tα1 treatment showed the most significant effect. Besides, combination treatment with Gem and Tα1 markedly inhibited cell growth and EMT progress, and enhanced apoptosis and autophagy. Similarly, Gem combined with Tα1 suppressed tumor growth, promoted apoptosis and autophagy in vivo. Additionally, combination treatment with Gem and Tα1 inhibited PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. In summary, combination administration of Gem and Tα1 suppressed the progression of NNKTL in vivo and in vitro. Our study provided an effective therapeutic strategy potentially for the clinical treatment of NNKTL.

studies.title: Thymosin alpha-1; a natural peptide inhibits cellular proliferation, cell migration, the level of reactive oxygen species and promotes the activity of antioxida
studies.abstract: This research was conducted to investigate the biochemical effects of thymosin alpha-1 using human lung cancer cells (A549). The A549 cells were treated with different concentrations of Thα1 for 24 h and the growth, inhibition of cells was determined. Thα1 revealed anti-proliferative effect at 24 and 48 μg/ml after 24 h. Furthermore, it indicated antioxidant properties by significantly enhancing the activity of catalase (12 μg/ml), superoxide dismutase (6 and 12 μg/ml), and glutathione peroxidase (3, 6 and 12 μg/ml) and reducing the production of cellular ROS. Our results showed that Thα1 inhibits the migration of A549 cells in a concentration-dependent manner after 24 and 48 h. Moreover, the effect of Thα1 on apoptosis was investigated by Hoechst 33342 staining and cell cycle analysis. Results demonstrated no significant effect on the induction of apoptosis in A549 cells. In conclusion, our results showed the antioxidant properties of Thα1 on A549 cancer cells.

studies.title: Generation of a novel long-acting thymosin alpha1-Fc fusion protein and its efficacy for the inhibition of breast cancer in vivo.
studies.abstract: Thymosin alpha1 (Tα1) is a multifunctional polypeptide involved in immunoregulation, which universally exists in various organs. The clinical application, however, is limited because of its short half-life. The Fc domain of human IgG has functional properties, improving the affinity and serum half-life. In this study, we fused Tα1 to Fc domain of human IgG1 for generation of a novel long-acting fusion protein, termed Tα1-Fc. Tα1-Fc was expressed, purified, and identified. The results showed that Tα1-Fc was more potent than Tα1 in inhibiting the growth of 4T1 and MCF-7 breast cancer cells in vivo. Furthermore, in the 4T1 tumor model the mice treated with Tα1-Fc exhibited higher level of CD4 and CD8 cells compared with that of the mice Tα1 treated. The interferon-γ and interleukin-2 level in the Tα1-Fc-treated mice was higher than that in the Tα1-treated mice. Tα1-Fc could also alleviate immunosuppression induced by hydrocortisone. In summary, Tα1-Fc provides a novel potent strategy to recruit immune cells against tumors and enhance the antitumor activity of Tα1.

studies.title: [Triplet anti-tumor therapy based on thymosin α-1 attenuates incidence of hepatoma and serum alpha-fetoprotein level in rat hepatoma model].
studies.abstract: To explore the impact of triple anti-tumor therapy based on thymosin α1 (Tα1) combined with Huaier granule(HG) and sirolimus on the level of serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) in rat models of liver cancer. Ninety Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly divided into triple anti-tumor therapy group, Tα1 group, HG group, sirolimus group, positive control and blank control groups, with 15 rats in each group. Except the blank control group, the rats in the other groups were induced using diethylnitrosamine (DEN) to establish liver cancer models. After DEN treatment, the triple therapy group underwent 0.8 mg/kg Tα1 subcutaneous injection (from once a day for two weeks to twice a week since the third week), 0.35 g/kg HG gavage (three times a day) and 1 mg/kg sirolimus gavage (once a day). The dose of the rest single drug groups were the same with that of the triple therapy group. The positive control and blank control groups were not treated with the drugs. The treatment lasted 20 weeks. Then, the behavior of the rats were observed at the different time points, and the level of serum AFP in the rats were detected at 6, 16, 18, 20 weeks, respectively. The typical symptoms of liver cancer were seen in the DEN-induced rats at 16 weeks. Since the tenth week, 6 rats died one after another. Pathological section of rat liver tissue suggested that the rat models were established successfully. According to the incidence rate of liver cancer and the survival rate at 20 weeks, the triple anti-tumor therapy was significantly superior to the single drug treatments. In addition, the triple anti-tumor therapy significantly reduced the level of serum AFP in the rats. The triple anti-tumor therapy can significantly prolong the survival time of rats with liver cancer, decrease the cancer incidence rate and the level of serum AFP.

studies.title: Thymosin alpha 1 suppresses proliferation and induces apoptosis in breast cancer cells through PTEN-mediated inhibition of PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway.
studies.abstract: Thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1), an immunoactive peptide, has been shown to inhibit cell proliferation and induce apoptosis in human leukemia, non-small cell lung cancer, melanoma, and other human cancers. However, the response and molecular mechanism of breast cancer cells exposed to Tα1 remain unclear. PTEN, a tumor suppressor gene, is frequently mutated in a variety of human cancers. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the biological roles of PTEN in the growth inhibition of human breast cancer cells exposed to Tα1. Using wild-type and mutant PTEN-expressing cells, we found a strong correlation between PTEN status and Tα1-mediated growth inhibition of breast cancer cells. The growth inhibition effect was more pronounced in breast cancer cells in which Tα1 enhanced PTEN expression, whereas endogenous PTEN knockdown reversed the growth inhibition effect of Tα1 in breast cancer cells. Further investigation revealed that PTEN up-regulation, which was induced by Tα1, can inhibit the activation of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway, leading to the growth inhibition of breast cancer cells. The addition of the synergy between Tα1 and the inhibition of PI3K/Akt/mTOR activation could strongly block cell viability in PTEN down-regulated breast cancer cells. PTEN-overexpressing cells not only up-regulated Bax and cleaved caspase-3/9 and PARP expression but also down-regulated Bcl-2 compared to the treatment with Tα1 alone. Together these findings suggest that PTEN mediates Tα1-induced apoptosis through the mitochondrial death cascade and inhibition of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway in breast cancer cells.

studies.title: A modified thymosin alpha 1 inhibits the growth of breast cancer both in vitro and in vivo: suppressment of cell proliferation, inducible cell apoptosis and enh
studies.abstract: Thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1) is commonly used for treating several diseases; however its usage has been limited because of poor penetration of the target tissue, such as tumor cells. In the present study, Tα1-iRGD, a peptide by conjugating Tα1 with the iRGD fragment, was evaluated its performance in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 human breast cancer cells. Compared with the wild-type peptide, Tα1-iRGD was more selective in binding tumor cells in the cell attachment assay. Furthermore, the MTT assay confirmed that Tα1-iRGD proved more effective in significantly inhibiting the growth of MCF-7 cells in contrast to the general inhibition displayed by Tα1. Further, conjugation of Tα1 with iRGD preserved the immunomodulatory activity of the drug by increasing the proliferation of mouse spleen lymphocytes. Further, compared with Tα1 treatment, Tα1-iRGD treatment of MCF-7 cells considerably increased the number of cells undergoing apoptosis, resulting in a dose-dependent inhibition of cancer cell growth, which was associated with a much better effect on up-regulation of the expression of BCL2-associated X protein (Bax), caspase 9, etc. More importantly, treatment with Ta1-iRGD was more efficacious than treatment with Ta1 in vivo. This study highlights the importance of iRGD on enhancement of cell penetration and tumor accumulation. In summary, our findings demonstrate that the novel modified Tα1 developed in this study has the potential to be used for treating breast cancer.

studies.title: Effect of thymosin alpha-1 on subpopulations of Th1, Th2, Th17, and regulatory T cells (Tregs) in vitro.
studies.abstract: Thymosin alpha 1 (Tα1) has been shown to have beneficial effects on numerous immune system parameters, but little is known about the effects of Tα1 on patients with gastric carcinoma. The objective of this study was to determine the effect of Tα1 on subpopulations of Th1, Th2, Th17, and regulatory T cells (Tregs) in vitro, and to evaluate its efficacy as an immunoregulatory factor in patients with gastric carcinoma. We compared the effect of Tα1 on the frequency of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, especially the CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from gastric carcinoma patients (N = 35) and healthy donors (N = 22). We also analyzed the changes in the proliferation of PBMCs in response to treatment with Tα1, and examined the production of Th1, Th2, and Th17 cytokines by PBMCs and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. The treatment of PBMCs from gastric cancer patients, with Tα1 (50 µg/mL) alone increased the percentage of CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ (suppressive antitumor-specific Tregs) from 1.68 ± 0.697 to 2.19 ± 0.795% (P < 0.05). Our results indicate that Tα1 increases the percentage of Tregs and IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 in vitro.

studies.title: [Effects of thymosin alpha-1 on radiation-induced pneumonitis].
studies.abstract:
Background and objective

Radiation-induced lung injure is one of the major factors of limitation in radiotherapy for lung cancer. Whether the use of thymosin and radiotherapy simultaneously would increase the radiation-induced lung injure is unclear. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of thymosin alpha-1 on radiation induced pneumonitis in mice.

Methods

Three groups of mice, control (C), radiation alone (RT), thymosin alpha-1 plus radiation (T+RT), were entered into the study. The weight and mortality of mice, pleural effusion, quantity of protein and cell count in the bronchoalvealar lavage (BAL) and pulmonary fibrosis score were evaluated as the outcome measures.

Results

The mortality ratio of the T+RT and RT groups were 3/14, 2/10, respectively. The time of death were all in the 23-24 weeks after radiotherapy. There was no pleural effusion in the T+RT group other than 2/2 occurred in RT group. The quantity of protein, cell number and neutrophil number in the BAL and lung coefficient in mice of T+RT group were remarkably lower than that of RT group, but the BALF macrophages number was remarkably higher than that in RT group in the 8 weeks. The quantity of protein, cell number, neutrophil number and macrophages number in the BAL, lung coefficient, the scores of lung fibrosis in mice of T+RT group were significantly lower than that of RT group in the 24 weeks. All test data were lowest in mice of C group. And there was no obvious pulmonary fibrosis in the mice of C group.

Conclusions

Thymosin alpha-1 could relieve radiation-induced acute and late pulmonary injuries.

studies.title: IRX-2 and thymosin alpha1 (Zadaxin) increase T lymphocytes in T lymphocytopenic mice and humans.
studies.abstract: Mouse studies showed a synergy of thymosin alpha1 (Talpha1) and a natural cytokine mixture (IRX-2) in increasing T lymphocyte number and responses. Clinical studies with IRX-2 showed increases of T lymphocytes in lymphocytopenic cancer patients but relatively little effect on irradiated, lymphocytopenic patients. The present phase 1 and 2 study shows that Talpha1 enhances the effect of IRX-2 in these lymphocytopenic patients. Patients (seven) were treated with subcutaneously injected IRX-2 (200 units IL-2 equivalence), Talpha1 (1.6 mg/day) (four patients), or the combination of IRX-2 and Talpha1 (seven patients) daily for 10 days. Peripheral blood lymphocytes (T, B, NK) and subsets (CD4, CD8) were measured at the start of treatment and on day 11. IRX-2 and Talpha1 had little or no significant effect. The combination markedly increased various lymphocyte populations (>350 cells/microL). Four patients followed for 6 weeks displayed sustained increases involving both naïve and memory T cells. Responses to persistent infections were observed in three of the four patients and no significant toxicity was observed. Talpha1 and IRX-2 synergize to increase safely T cells in lymphocytopenic patients.

studies.title: Immunopharmacology of thymosin alpha1 and cytokine synergy.
studies.abstract: Thymosin alpha1 (Talpha1) is a 28 amino acid biologically active protein cleaved from positions 2-29 of a precursor protein, prothymosin alpha. Since its discovery, Talpha1 has been administered to animals and humans in a wide variety of settings and its pharmacologic effects are to enhance cellular immunity. Talpha1 administration is highly effective in settings where irradiation, chemotherapy, tumor burden, or immune senescence have caused a reduction of T cell number and/or function. Recent in vitro studies, including the one reported here, suggest that Talpha1 may act via pathways commonly used by various cytokines. This raises the possibility that Talpha1 and cytokines may have synergistic activity through potentiation of cytokine activity by Talpha1. Improved control of tumor growth when tumor-bearing mice were treated with Talpha1 and high doses of IL-2 has been previously reported. We extended those studies with the Lewis lung carcinoma mouse model using IRX-2, a natural well-defined biologic containing multiple cytokines, in combination with Talpha1 (IRX-3). Although IRX-2 was effective alone (using doses that contain significantly less IL-2 than in most typical studies), adding Talpha1 led to significant improvement in survival of the tumor-bearing mice. Based on these observations, the immunopharmacology of Talpha1 predicts an important clinical role for Talpha1 in the restoration of cellular immune activity when used in combination with cytokines. Patients who experience immune suppression due to the presence of tumor, irradiation, and/or chemotherapy or aging of the host would most benefit from this treatment combination.

studies.title: Combination therapy with thymosin alpha 1 potentiates the anti-tumor activity of interleukin-2 with cyclophosphamide in the treatment of the Lewis lung carcinom
studies.abstract: In this study we have investigated the effects of thymosin alpha 1 (T alpha 1) and interleukin-2 (IL-2), singly or in combination with cyclophosphamide (CY), on tumor growth, survival and cytotoxicity in C57Bl/6NCrlBR mice with Lewis lung carcinoma (3LL). Combined administration of T alpha 1 plus IL-2, after CY treatment, was much more effective than use of each biological response modifier (BRM) alone, and induced complete tumor regression in all of the mice studied. Combination immunotherapy alone without CY only slightly reduced the rate of tumor growth, and these results are in accordance with previous studied which showed that the 3LL carcinoma is resistant to cytokines. Combined chemo-immunotherapy also increased the cytotoxicity of spleen cells and markedly enhanced long-term survival in all treated animals. Depletion of immune cells, using either total-body sub-lethal irradiation (400 rads) or antibodies directed against T-cell (anti-CD4 and CD8) or NK-cell (anti-asialo GM1) populations, abolished the positive response to combination therapy. Histological analysis of the tumors obtained from mice treated with combination chemo-immunotherapy revealed a high number of infiltrating lymphoid cells surrounding a well-circumscribed area of necrosis consisting solely of dead cells. Our studies show that T alpha 1 potentiates IL-2-induced cytotoxic activities in vitro as well in vivo, and that these compounds have a powerful anti-tumor action when associated with chemotherapy.

studies.title: Immunopotentiator thymosin alpha-1 attenuates inflammatory pain by modulating the Wnt3a/β-catenin pathway in spinal cord.
studies.abstract: The mechanism of inflammatory pain involves the central nervous system (CNS) and the immune system. It is reported that immunopotentiator thymosin alpha-1 (Tα1) can reduce inflammation, protect neurons and strengthen the immune function. However, the roles of Tα1 in inflammatory pain still remain unclear. In this study, we found Tα1 can attenuate the complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced mechanical allodynia and heat hyperalgesia. Meanwhile, it reduced the upregulation of CFA-induced inflammatory mediators (interferon (IFN)-γ, tumor necrosis factor-α and brain-derived neurotrophic factor). In addition, we found the Wnt3a/β-catenin pathway was activated in spinal cord after the injection of CFA, paralleling with pain hypersensitivity. However, Tα1 reversed this status. In summary, Tα1 could attenuate inflammatory pain by modulating the Wnt3a/β-catenin pathway. It might be related to the downregulation of inflammatory mediators.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A 28-amino-acid peptide that mimics a naturally occurring immune signaling molecule.
explanation.what_it_is: Thymosin alpha-1 is a small peptide—a chain of 28 amino acids (the building blocks of proteins)—with a molecular weight of 3,108 daltons. It is derived from the thymus, a gland in your chest that trains immune cells called T cells. The compound is administered by injection, typically subcutaneously (under the skin). It is also known as Thymalfasin and is classified as a research peptide in many jurisdictions.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates and trains immune cells, particularly T cells, to better recognize and fight pathogens and abnormal cells.
explanation.how_it_works: Thymosin alpha-1 works primarily by signaling to T cells—immune cells that are central to fighting infections and recognizing cancer. It binds to receptors (docking points) on the surface of T cells and immune dendritic cells, triggering them to mature, proliferate, and become more active. This activation boosts the production of immune signaling molecules called cytokines (chemical messengers between immune cells) and enhances the T cells' ability to recognize and attack pathogens or abnormal cells. The peptide also promotes the balance of different T cell subsets, helping the immune system respond in a coordinated way. Because it is very water-soluble (XLogP −24), it does not cross cell membranes easily and acts on cell surface receptors, making it a systemic immune signal rather than an intracellular drug.
explanation.safety_line: Reported as generally well-tolerated in short-term trials; long-term safety and rare effects remain incompletely characterized.
explanation.safety_detail: Most retrieved trials of thymosin alpha-1 reported mild or no adverse effects, with injection-site reactions and minor systemic symptoms (headache, fatigue) documented in small numbers. However, the trials reviewed were predominantly short-term (weeks to a few months), and the populations tested were largely adults with specific conditions (hepatitis, infection, cancer). Long-term safety profiles, effects in children or adolescents, and use during pregnancy have not been adequately studied in the records provided.
safety_bullets: Pregnancy and lactation: not tested in retrieved trials; unknown safety
Pediatric and adolescent use: excluded from nearly all retrieved studies; untested in children
Chronic administration beyond several months: limited data; most trials were short-term
Drug interactions: not systematically evaluated in the studies provided; unknown
explanation.chem_meaning: Thymosin alpha-1 is an extremely water-loving molecule (XLogP −24), meaning it dissolves readily in water and cannot easily cross cell membranes to enter the cell interior. This hydrophilic nature means it works by binding to receptors on the cell surface rather than acting inside the cell, and it remains largely confined to the bloodstream and extracellular spaces. Its large size (3,108 Da) and peptide structure also make it susceptible to breakdown by proteases (protein-cutting enzymes) in the digestive tract, which is why it must be injected rather than taken orally.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Meta-analyses and systematic reviews spanning 30 human studies (n=1,144 or larger across pooled analyses) and 17 animal studies consistently show that thymosin alpha-1 enhances immune function, with a pooled mean difference of 7.54 (95% CI 6.66–8.41). Key human evidence includes a 2020 meta-analysis (n=1,144) on hepatitis B treatment, a 2025 systematic review (n=706) on severe acute pancreatitis, a 2024 systematic review (n=329) on acute exacerbation of COPD, a 2023 review (n=19) on COVID-19, and an open-label study suggesting antidepressive effects. Five independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converge on this outcome, indicating robust consistency across diverse clinical populations.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong evidence grade is supported by adequately powered human studies, consistency across five independent syntheses, and diverse disease contexts (hepatitis, pancreatitis, COPD, COVID-19, sepsis). The effect size is clinically meaningful and replicable across independent research teams.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Twenty-one human studies and six animal studies demonstrate efficacy in infection and sepsis management. Key human evidence includes a 2020 meta-analysis (n=1,144) on hepatitis B, a 2025 systematic review (n=706) on pancreatitis-related infection, a 2025 RCT (n=1,106) on sepsis (the TESTS trial, multicentre, double-blinded, placebo-controlled), and a 2023 pilot RCT (n=49) on hospitalized hypoxemic patients with low lymphocyte counts. Four independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converge, indicating replicable protective effects.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong grade reflects 21 human studies with consistent results, large sample sizes in pooled analyses, inclusion of rigorous RCTs (including a recent large multicentre placebo-controlled trial), and convergence across four independent meta-analyses. The evidence spans both acute infection and chronic viral hepatitis, supporting broad efficacy.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ten human studies and three animal studies examine liver outcomes, with a pooled odds ratio of 3.71 (95% CI 2.05–6.71). Human evidence includes a 2020 meta-analysis (n=1,144) comparing entecavir plus thymosin alpha-1 versus entecavir alone in hepatitis B, a 2008 meta-analysis comparing thymosin alpha-1 to interferon-alpha, a 2022 RCT (n=120) on hepatitis B-related acute-on-chronic liver failure, a 2012 RCT (n=552) on hepatitis C, and a 1996 double-blind placebo-controlled pilot (n not specified) on chronic hepatitis C. Two pooled analyses and seven primary human trials constitute the human evidence base.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade is assigned because only seven primary human studies and two pooled analyses were retrieved—below the threshold for strong tier. While the pooled effect is substantial and consistent across hepatitis B and C contexts, the human evidence base is more limited than for immune function or sepsis. The outcome is well-supported but would benefit from additional independent trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Thirteen human studies and fifteen animal studies examine cancer and tumor outcomes. Human evidence includes a 2024 RCT (n=400) on perioperative immune function in cancer surgery, a 2022 RCT (n=69) on radiation pneumonitis in non-small-cell lung cancer, a 2015 multicentre RCT on cancer, a 2010 large randomized study combining thymosin alpha-1 with interferon-alpha and dacarbazine in melanoma, a 2008 RCT on tooth reimplantation (n not specified in abstract), and a 2023 study (n=19) on lymphocyte immune homeostasis in long COVID. Across nine studies with disclosed sample sizes, 7,144+ participants are documented; most abstracts omit total enrollment, so the true denominator is substantially larger.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects inconsistency: while 13 human and 15 animal studies exist, no single pooled meta-analysis confirms agreement across all trials. Studies span diverse cancers and endpoints (immune function, radiation side effects, survival proxy markers), making homogenization difficult. The evidence is promising but heterogeneous; held at moderate pending formal quantitative synthesis. Precision is also limited by the fact that most abstracts do not report sample sizes.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base for thymosin alpha-1 is predominantly human: 74 human studies and 41 animal studies are represented in the records provided. Human evidence includes multiple meta-analyses (particularly convergent syntheses for immune function, infection, and liver outcomes), numerous RCTs spanning hepatitis B and C, sepsis, COVID-19, COPD, pancreatitis, and cancer, and some observational studies. Most human trials are from the past two decades (2008–2025), with the most recent evidence from 2025. Animal studies support mechanistic plausibility. This means the evidence is both recent and clinically grounded, though some outcomes remain heterogeneous and await unified synthesis.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided show strong evidence in adults with viral hepatitis, sepsis, and respiratory/infectious conditions, but several populations are underrepresented or absent: pediatric and adolescent users are almost entirely excluded from the trials retrieved; long-term safety beyond a few months is not systematically reported; and chronic/maintenance dosing regimens are not well-characterized. Cancer outcomes rest on diverse study designs and populations (lung cancer, melanoma, surgical immunosuppression) without a unified meta-analysis, leaving mechanistic understanding and comparative efficacy unclear. Additionally, optimal dosing, frequency of administration, and whether benefits persist after cessation of therapy are not comprehensively addressed in the records available. Note: these gaps reflect the sample of ~40 abstracts per outcome provided to this explainer; they do not characterize the entire published literature.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base conflates disease-adjacent outcomes (sepsis, acute pancreatitis, post-surgical immune markers) with genuine immune function, and rests heavily on studies from China with limited disclosure of funding, blinding, or allocation concealment—warranting skepticism about effect size and applicability to healthy populations.

concerns.issue: Outcome definition creep and surrogate endpoints
concerns.detail: The 'immune function' outcome (graded Strong) pools heterogeneous proxies: lymphocyte counts, inflammatory markers, and T-cell populations in acutely ill hospitalized patients (pancreatitis, sepsis, COPD, COVID-19). None of these are direct measures of immune competence in healthy individuals, nor do they establish that the peptide prevents infection or disease in non-hospitalized populations. The pooled effect size (7.54 [6.66–8.41]) is presented as clinically meaningful, but the metric ('mean_diff') is not specified—it could represent percentage-point shifts in lab values that may not translate to clinical benefit.

concerns.issue: Geographic and design bias in primary evidence
concerns.detail: The infection/sepsis outcome (Strong grade) draws heavily from four meta-analyses that synthesize predominantly Chinese-authored RCTs (e.g., 2022 RCT n=508, 2024 RCT n=502 on pancreatitis; 2013 RCT n=361 on sepsis). Funding sources and conflict-of-interest statements are not visible in these records. Chinese pharmaceutical publications show systematically higher effect sizes and lower rates of reported adverse events than Western trials on identical interventions. Without access to allocation concealment, selective outcome reporting, or trial registration details, the apparent consistency across meta-analyses may reflect consistent bias rather than robust efficacy.

concerns.issue: No direct evidence in asymptomatic or non-hospitalized populations
concerns.detail: Every human RCT in the retrieved records enrolls acutely ill patients: those with sepsis, acute pancreatitis, hepatitis B/C, COPD exacerbation, or COVID-19 pneumonia. The 2025 open-label RCT on depression (n not reported) is the sole study touching a non-infectious indication, but it is open-label and lacks a sample size descriptor. There is zero evidence that thymosin alpha-1 enhances immune function in healthy people, making extrapolation from hospitalized populations to self-administration in grey-market settings unfounded.

concerns.issue: Pooled effect sizes rest on a small number of large studies, with substantial heterogeneity unaddressed
concerns.detail: The infection/sepsis outcome (Strong, n=27 studies) reports 'consistency' across four meta-analyses, but no quantitative heterogeneity metric (I²) is provided in these records. The largest contributor, the 2025 TESTS trial (n=1106), is recent and presumably high-quality, but it is listed as a single RCT—if it drove the pooled result and had null or modest findings, the aggregate grade might be overstated. The 2020 meta-analysis (n=1144) on hepatitis B + entecavir is repeated across three outcome categories (immune function, infection, liver health), suggesting potential double-counting and inflating apparent consistency.

concerns.issue: Cancer/tumor outcome is underspecified and lacks pooled analysis
concerns.detail: The cancer outcome is graded Moderate, with a note that 'no pooled analysis confirms [studies] agree.' Of 28 studies, 14 are animal and 9 are unclassified (likely mechanistic or case reports), leaving only 5 human RCTs. Sample sizes are omitted for most abstracts; the largest (5746) is unclassified and likely an observational registry, not a trial. One RCT (2010) mixes thymosin alpha-1 with dacarbazine and interferon alfa, confounding attribution. Without a meta-analysis and with such sparse RCT evidence, claiming 'Moderate' grade—equivalent to the liver health outcome with 10 human studies—appears inconsistent.

concerns.issue: Adverse event and safety data absent from these records
concerns.detail: The records display titles mentioning 'safety and efficacy' (e.g., 2022 RCT on hepatitis B, 2025 TESTS trial), but no adverse event rates, serious adverse events, or discontinuation rates are summarized. An injectable peptide obtained grey-market carries potential risks (contamination, batch variability, allergic reaction, autoimmune flare). The absence of accessible safety data here means readers cannot weigh harm against the claimed benefits, particularly for healthy self-administered use.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanism is that thymosin alpha-1 stimulates T-cell maturation in the thymus, thereby enhancing adaptive immunity. The clinical outcomes in these trials—sepsis mortality, pancreatitis-related organ dysfunction, hepatitis B viral clearance—are plausibly downstream of improved immune response and are not implausible. However, the leap from lab measures of immune activation (lymphocyte count, T-cell subsets) in hospitalized acute illness to clinical benefit in healthy individuals is large and not bridged by any study in these records. Hospitalized patients have transient immune suppression; the degree to which restoring it in acutely ill patients generalizes to chronic immune enhancement in the asymptomatic is unknown.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptical expert would note that (1) all human RCT evidence comes from acutely hospitalized patients with specific infections or organ dysfunction, and thymosin alpha-1 may simply restore transiently suppressed immunity to baseline rather than enhance it above normal; (2) the evidence base is dominated by small-to-medium Chinese trials with limited transparency on methods, and meta-analyses may be amplifying consistent bias rather than measuring true effect; (3) the single largest recent trial (2025 TESTS, n=1106) appears in the infection/sepsis listing but is not highlighted as the primary basis for the Strong grade, raising questions about whether its results truly support the pooled claims or whether older, smaller studies are being overweighted for consistency.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A well-powered, Western-conducted, double-blind RCT in healthy volunteers (n≥200) with pre-specified immune markers, infection incidence over 12+ months, and full trial registration and adverse-event disclosure would directly test whether thymosin alpha-1 enhances immune function outside the acute-illness setting. Alternatively, a rigorous individual-patient-data meta-analysis of existing RCTs with stratification by baseline immune status and explicit assessment of study-level bias would clarify whether the apparent consistency reflects genuine efficacy or methodological artifacts.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido de 28 aminoácidos que imita una molécula natural de señalización inmunológica.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Timosina alfa-1 es un pequeño péptido—una cadena de 28 aminoácidos (los bloques de construcción de las proteínas)—con un peso molecular de 3,108 daltons. Se deriva del timo, una glándula en el pecho que entrena células inmunológicas llamadas células T. El compuesto se administra por inyección, típicamente por vía subcutánea (bajo la piel). También se conoce como Timalfasin y se clasifica como un péptido de investigación en muchas jurisdicciones.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa y entrena células inmunológicas, particularmente células T, para reconocer y combatir mejor los patógenos y las células anormales.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Timosina alfa-1 funciona principalmente al señalizar a las células T—células inmunológicas que son centrales para combatir infecciones y reconocer el cáncer. Se une a receptores (puntos de anclaje) en la superficie de las células T y las células dendríticas inmunológicas, desencadenando que maduren, se proliferen y se vuelvan más activas. Esta activación aumenta la producción de moléculas de señalización inmunológica llamadas citoquinas (mensajeros químicos entre células inmunológicas) y mejora la capacidad de las células T para reconocer y atacar patógenos o células anormales. El péptido también promueve el equilibrio de diferentes subconjuntos de células T, ayudando al sistema inmunológico a responder de manera coordinada. Debido a que es muy soluble en agua (XLogP −24), no cruza fácilmente las membranas celulares y actúa sobre receptores en la superficie celular, lo que lo convierte en una señal inmunológica sistémica en lugar de un fármaco intracelular.
explanation_es.safety_line: Reportado como generalmente bien tolerado en ensayos a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo y los efectos raros permanecen incompletamente caracterizados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: La mayoría de los ensayos recuperados de timosina alfa-1 reportaron efectos adversos leves o ausentes, con reacciones en el sitio de inyección y síntomas sistémicos menores (dolor de cabeza, fatiga) documentados en pequeños números. Sin embargo, los ensayos revisados fueron predominantemente a corto plazo (semanas a algunos meses), y las poblaciones probadas fueron en gran medida adultos con condiciones específicas (hepatitis, infección, cáncer). Los perfiles de seguridad a largo plazo, los efectos en niños o adolescentes, y el uso durante el embarazo no han sido estudiados adecuadamente en los registros proporcionados.
safety_bullets: Embarazo y lactancia: no probado en ensayos recuperados; seguridad desconocida
Uso pediátrico y adolescente: excluido de casi todos los estudios recuperados; no probado en niños
Administración crónica más allá de varios meses: datos limitados; la mayoría de los ensayos fueron a corto plazo
Interacciones farmacológicas: no evaluadas sistemáticamente en los estudios proporcionados; desconocidas
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Timosina alfa-1 es una molécula extremadamente hidrófila (XLogP −24), lo que significa que se disuelve fácilmente en agua y no puede cruzar fácilmente las membranas celulares para entrar en el interior celular. Esta naturaleza hidrofílica significa que funciona al unirse a receptores en la superficie celular en lugar de actuar dentro de la célula, y permanece en gran medida confinada al torrente sanguíneo y los espacios extracelulares. Su tamaño grande (3,108 Da) y estructura de péptido también la hacen susceptible a la degradación por proteasas (enzimas que cortan proteínas) en el tracto digestivo, por lo que debe inyectarse en lugar de tomarse por vía oral.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas que abarcan 30 estudios humanos (n=1,144 o mayor en análisis agrupados) y 17 estudios animales muestran consistentemente que timosina alfa-1 mejora la función inmunológica, con una diferencia media agrupada de 7.54 (IC 95% 6.66–8.41). La evidencia humana clave incluye un metanálisis de 2020 (n=1,144) sobre tratamiento de hepatitis B, una revisión sistemática de 2025 (n=706) sobre pancreatitis aguda grave, una revisión sistemática de 2024 (n=329) sobre exacerbación aguda de EPOC, una revisión de 2023 (n=19) sobre COVID-19, y un estudio de etiqueta abierta sugiriendo efectos antidepresivos. Cinco metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas independientes convergen en este resultado, indicando consistencia robusta en diversas poblaciones clínicas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación de evidencia fuerte está respaldada por estudios humanos adecuadamente potenciados, consistencia entre cinco síntesis independientes, y contextos de enfermedades diversas (hepatitis, pancreatitis, EPOC, COVID-19, sepsis). El tamaño del efecto es clínicamente significativo y replicable en equipos de investigación independientes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Veintiún estudios humanos y seis estudios animales demuestran eficacia en el manejo de infecciones y sepsis. La evidencia humana clave incluye un metanálisis de 2020 (n=1,144) sobre hepatitis B, una revisión sistemática de 2025 (n=706) sobre infección relacionada con pancreatitis, un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2025 (n=1,106) sobre sepsis (el ensayo TESTS, multicéntrico, doble ciego, controlado con placebo), y un ensayo controlado aleatorizado piloto de 2023 (n=49) sobre pacientes hospitalizados hipoxémicos con recuentos bajos de linfocitos. Cuatro metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas independientes convergen, indicando efectos protectores replicables.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación fuerte refleja 21 estudios humanos con resultados consistentes, tamaños de muestra grandes en análisis agrupados, inclusión de ensayos rigurosos controlados aleatorios (incluyendo un ensayo multicéntrico reciente controlado con placebo), y convergencia en cuatro metanálisis independientes. La evidencia abarca tanto infección aguda como hepatitis viral crónica, apoyando eficacia amplia.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Diez estudios humanos y tres estudios animales examinan resultados hepáticos, con una razón de probabilidades agrupada de 3.71 (IC 95% 2.05–6.71). La evidencia humana incluye un metanálisis de 2020 (n=1,144) comparando entecavir más timosina alfa-1 versus entecavir solo en hepatitis B, un metanálisis de 2008 comparando timosina alfa-1 con interferón-alfa, un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2022 (n=120) sobre insuficiencia hepática aguda sobre crónica relacionada con hepatitis B, un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2012 (n=552) sobre hepatitis C, y un piloto doble ciego controlado con placebo de 1996 (n no especificado) sobre hepatitis C crónica. Dos análisis agrupados y siete ensayos primarios humanos constituyen la base de evidencia humana.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada se asigna porque solo se recuperaron siete estudios humanos primarios y dos análisis agrupados—por debajo del umbral para el nivel fuerte. Si bien el efecto agrupado es sustancial y consistente en contextos de hepatitis B y C, la base de evidencia humana es más limitada que para función inmunológica o sepsis. El resultado está bien respaldado pero se beneficiaría de ensayos independientes adicionales.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Trece estudios humanos y quince estudios animales examinan resultados de cáncer y tumor. La evidencia humana incluye un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2024 (n=400) sobre función inmunológica perioperatoria en cirugía del cáncer, un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2022 (n=69) sobre neumonitis por radiación en cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas, un ensayo multicéntrico controlado aleatorizado de 2015 sobre cáncer, un gran estudio aleatorizado de 2010 combinando timosina alfa-1 con interferón-alfa y dacarbazina en melanoma, un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 2008 sobre reimplante dentario (n no especificado en el resumen), y un estudio de 2023 (n=19) sobre homeostasis inmunológica de linfocitos en COVID prolongado. En nueve estudios con tamaños de muestra divulgados, se documentan 7,144+ participantes; la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten la inscripción total, por lo que el denominador verdadero es sustancialmente mayor.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja inconsistencia: mientras que existen 13 estudios humanos y 15 estudios animales, ningún metanálisis agrupado único confirma acuerdo en todos los ensayos. Los estudios abarcan cánceres diversos y puntos finales (función inmunológica, efectos secundarios de la radiación, marcadores proxy de supervivencia), lo que dificulta la homogeneización. La evidencia es prometedora pero heterogénea; se mantiene en moderada pendiente de síntesis cuantitativa formal. La precisión también es limitada por el hecho de que la mayoría de los resúmenes no reportan tamaños de muestra.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia para timosina alfa-1 es predominantemente humana: 74 estudios humanos y 41 estudios animales están representados en los registros proporcionados. La evidencia humana incluye múltiples metanálisis (particularmente síntesis convergentes para función inmunológica, infección, y resultados hepáticos), numerosos ensayos controlados aleatorios que abarcan hepatitis B y C, sepsis, COVID-19, EPOC, pancreatitis y cáncer, y algunos estudios observacionales. La mayoría de los ensayos humanos son de las últimas dos décadas (2008–2025), con la evidencia más reciente de 2025. Los estudios animales apoyan la plausibilidad mecanicista. Esto significa que la evidencia es tanto reciente como clínicamente fundamentada, aunque algunos resultados permanecen heterogéneos y aguardan síntesis unificada.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran evidencia fuerte en adultos con hepatitis viral, sepsis y condiciones respiratorias/infecciosas, pero varias poblaciones están subrepresentadas o ausentes: los usuarios pediátricos y adolescentes están casi completamente excluidos de los ensayos recuperados; la seguridad a largo plazo más allá de algunos meses no se reporta sistemáticamente; y los regímenes de dosificación crónica/mantenimiento no están bien caracterizados. Los resultados del cáncer se basan en diseños de estudios diversos y poblaciones (cáncer de pulmón, melanoma, inmunosupresión quirúrgica) sin un metanálisis unificado, dejando la comprensión mecanicista y la eficacia comparativa poco claras. Además, la dosis óptima, la frecuencia de administración, y si los beneficios persisten después del cese de la terapia no se abordan de manera integral en los registros disponibles. Nota: estas brechas reflejan la muestra de ~40 resúmenes por resultado proporcionada a este explicador; no caracterizan la literatura publicada completa.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia confunde resultados adyacentes a la enfermedad (sepsis, pancreatitis aguda, marcadores inmunológicos posquirúrgicos) con función inmunológica genuina, y se apoya fuertemente en estudios de China con divulgación limitada de financiamiento, enmascaramiento o ocultamiento de asignación—lo que justifica escepticismo sobre el tamaño del efecto y la aplicabilidad a poblaciones sanas.

concerns.issue: Cambio en la definición de resultados y puntos finales intermedios
concerns.detail: El resultado de 'función inmunológica' (clasificado Fuerte) agrupa proxies heterogéneos: recuentos de linfocitos, marcadores inflamatorios y poblaciones de células T en pacientes hospitalizados agudamente enfermos (pancreatitis, sepsis, EPOC, COVID-19). Ninguno de estos es una medida directa de competencia inmunológica en individuos sanos, ni establecen que el péptido prevenga infección o enfermedad en poblaciones no hospitalizadas. El tamaño del efecto agrupado (7.54 [6.66–8.41]) se presenta como clínicamente significativo, pero la métrica ('mean_diff') no está especificada—podría representar cambios en puntos porcentuales en valores de laboratorio que pueden no traducirse en beneficio clínico.

concerns.issue: Sesgo geográfico y de diseño en la evidencia primaria
concerns.detail: El resultado de infección/sepsis (clasificación Fuerte) se basa fuertemente en cuatro metanálisis que sintetizan predominantemente ensayos clínicos aleatorizados de autoría china (p. ej., RCT 2022 n=508, RCT 2024 n=502 sobre pancreatitis; RCT 2013 n=361 sobre sepsis). Las fuentes de financiamiento y declaraciones de conflicto de intereses no son visibles en estos registros. Las publicaciones farmacéuticas chinas muestran sistemáticamente tamaños de efecto más altos y tasas más bajas de eventos adversos reportados que los ensayos occidentales sobre intervenciones idénticas. Sin acceso a ocultamiento de asignación, reporte selectivo de resultados o detalles de registro de ensayos, la consistencia aparente entre metanálisis puede reflejar sesgo consistente más que eficacia robusta.

concerns.issue: Sin evidencia directa en poblaciones asintomáticas o no hospitalizadas
concerns.detail: Cada RCT humano en los registros recuperados incluye pacientes agudamente enfermos: aquellos con sepsis, pancreatitis aguda, hepatitis B/C, exacerbación de EPOC, o neumonía por COVID-19. El RCT abierto de 2025 sobre depresión (n no reportado) es el único estudio tocando una indicación no infecciosa, pero es abierto y carece de un descriptor de tamaño de muestra. Hay cero evidencia de que la timosina alfa-1 mejore la función inmunológica en personas sanas, haciendo infundada la extrapolación de poblaciones hospitalizadas a auto-administración en entornos de mercado gris.

concerns.issue: Los tamaños de efecto agrupados descansan en un pequeño número de estudios grandes, con heterogeneidad sustancial sin abordar
concerns.detail: El resultado de infección/sepsis (Fuerte, n=27 estudios) reporta 'consistencia' entre cuatro metanálisis, pero ninguna métrica de heterogeneidad cuantitativa (I²) se proporciona en estos registros. El contribuidor más grande, el ensayo TESTS 2025 (n=1106), es reciente y presumiblemente de alta calidad, pero se enumera como un solo RCT—si impulsó el resultado agrupado y tuvo hallazgos nulos o modestos, la clasificación agregada podría estar sobrestimada. El metanálisis de 2020 (n=1144) sobre hepatitis B + entecavir se repite entre tres categorías de resultados (función inmunológica, infección, salud hepática), sugiriendo double-counting potencial e inflando aparente consistencia.

concerns.issue: El resultado de cáncer/tumor está insuficientemente especificado y carece de análisis agrupado
concerns.detail: El resultado de cáncer se clasifica como Moderado, con una nota de que 'ningún análisis agrupado confirma [que los estudios] concuerden.' De 28 estudios, 14 son en animales y 9 no clasificados (probablemente mecanísticos o reportes de casos), dejando solo 5 RCTs humanos. Los tamaños de muestra se omiten para la mayoría de resúmenes; el más grande (5746) no se clasifica y probablemente es un registro observacional, no un ensayo. Un RCT (2010) mezcla timosina alfa-1 con dacarbazina e interferón alfa, confundiendo la atribución. Sin un metanálisis y con evidencia tan escasa de RCTs, reclamar una clasificación 'Moderada'—equivalente al resultado de salud hepática con 10 estudios humanos—parece inconsistente.

concerns.issue: Datos de eventos adversos y seguridad ausentes de estos registros
concerns.detail: Los registros muestran títulos mencionando 'seguridad y eficacia' (p. ej., RCT 2022 sobre hepatitis B, ensayo TESTS 2025), pero ninguna tasa de evento adverso, evento adverso serio, o tasas de discontinuación se resumen. Un péptido inyectable obtenido en mercado gris conlleva riesgos potenciales (contaminación, variabilidad de lote, reacción alérgica, brote autoinmunológico). La ausencia de datos de seguridad accesibles aquí significa que los lectores no pueden sopesar el daño contra los beneficios reclamados, particularmente para uso auto-administrado en sanos.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo propuesto es que la timosina alfa-1 estimula la maduración de células T en el timo, mejorando así la inmunidad adaptativa. Los resultados clínicos en estos ensayos—mortalidad por sepsis, disfunción de órganos relacionada con pancreatitis, aclaramiento viral de hepatitis B—son plausiblemente corriente abajo de una respuesta inmunológica mejorada y no son implausibles. Sin embargo, el salto de medidas de laboratorio de activación inmunológica (recuento de linfocitos, subconjuntos de células T) en enfermedad aguda hospitalizada a beneficio clínico en individuos sanos es grande y no está bridado por ningún estudio en estos registros. Los pacientes hospitalizados tienen supresión inmunológica transitoria; el grado en que restaurarla en pacientes agudamente enfermos se generaliza a mejora inmunológica crónica en asintomáticos es desconocido.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un experto escéptico señalaría que (1) toda la evidencia de RCT humano proviene de pacientes agudamente hospitalizados con infecciones específicas o disfunción de órganos, y la timosina alfa-1 puede simplemente restaurar la inmunidad transitoriamente suprimida a línea de base en lugar de mejorarla por encima de lo normal; (2) la base de evidencia está dominada por ensayos chinos pequeños a medianos con transparencia limitada en métodos, y los metanálisis pueden estar amplificando sesgo consistente en lugar de medir efecto verdadero; (3) el único ensayo reciente más grande (2025 TESTS, n=1106) aparece en el listado de infección/sepsis pero no se destaca como la base principal para la clasificación Fuerte, planteando preguntas sobre si sus resultados realmente apoyan los reclamos agrupados u si estudios más antiguos y pequeños están siendo sobrepesados por consistencia.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un RCT doble-ciego bien potenciado, conducido en Occidente, en voluntarios sanos (n≥200) con marcadores inmunológicos preespecificados, incidencia de infección durante 12+ meses, y registro de ensayo completo y divulgación de eventos adversos probaría directamente si la timosina alfa-1 mejora la función inmunológica fuera del contexto de enfermedad aguda. Alternativamente, un metanálisis riguroso de datos de pacientes individuales de RCTs existentes con estratificación por estado inmunológico basal y evaluación explícita de sesgo a nivel de estudio esclarecería si la aparente consistencia refleja eficacia genuina o artefactos metodológicos.
